title: Light and Sound Waves
seo_title: Grade 8 Light and Sound Waves Worksheets: Reflection, Absorption, Transmission and Refraction
standard_text: Develop and use a model to describe that waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through various materials.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on light and sound waves (NGSS MS-PS4-2): reflection, absorption and transmission, transparent and opaque materials, color, refraction, echoes and the speed of sound. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Waves are reflected, absorbed or transmitted.
key_sub: Light can cross empty space and bends between materials. Sound needs matter and is fastest in solids.
body_html:
How to think about it

When a wave reaches a new material, it can be reflected (bounce back), absorbed (taken in, often becoming heat) or transmitted (pass through). Often all three happen.

  • Light travels even through empty space. A mirror reflects it at the same angle it hits (angle in = angle out). Light refracts (bends) when it moves into a new material. Materials are transparent, translucent or opaque. We see the colors an object reflects.
  • Sound needs a medium. It travels fastest in solids and slowest in gases. Echoes are reflected sound; soft materials absorb sound.
Example

A ray hits a mirror at 40° from the normal. Reflection angle?

Angle in = angle out.

Answer: 40°

Example

Why does a green leaf look green?

We see reflected colors.

Answer: It reflects green light and absorbs the others.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sound can travel through empty space.
  • Thinking a red object absorbs red light. It reflects red.
  • Thinking sound is fastest in air. It is fastest in solids.

faq.q: What happens when light hits an object?
faq.a: The light can be reflected, absorbed or transmitted. The colors that are reflected are the colors we see.

faq.q: Why can't sound travel in space?
faq.a: Sound is a vibration of matter. Space has almost no matter, so there is nothing to carry the vibration.

faq.q: What is the law of reflection?
faq.a: The angle at which light hits a flat surface equals the angle at which it bounces off, both measured from the normal line.

items.q: Emma shouts toward a cliff and hears the echo 5 s later. Sound travels at about 343 m/s in air. How far away is the cliff?
